description: Anomaly-detector view. The state timeline classifies each backend per time bucket using the same threshold engine the anomaly-detector ships with (latency > 200 ms => degraded; error_rate > 5% => unhealthy). The threshold lines on the latency and error panels show how close each backend is to flipping. The leaderboard tallies time spent in each state over the visible window; the backend_health table panel shows the anomaly-detector's official verdicts straight from TimescaleDB.

panels.description: Per-backend state derived from raw metrics in the same way the threshold engine does. Green = healthy (within both thresholds), yellow = degraded (latency > 200 ms), red = unhealthy (error_rate > 5%). The strict-threshold view here may show 'healthy' while the anomaly-detector publishes 'degraded' via Redis — the detector uses STDDEV / MAX features in addition to mean. This panel is the raw-metric reference view; the table below carries the detector's actual verdicts.
panels.title: Backend health timeline (derived from threshold engine rules)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  time_bucket('$__interval', time) AS "time",
  instance AS metric,
  CASE
    WHEN AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE metric_name = 'error_rate')         > 0.05  THEN 'unhealthy'
    WHEN AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE metric_name = 'request_latency_ms') > 200   THEN 'degraded'
    ELSE 'healthy'
  END AS state
FROM metrics
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
  AND service = 'load-balancer'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.description: p95 latency per backend with the 200 ms DEGRADED threshold drawn as a red line. When a series crosses the line the threshold engine flips that backend to DEGRADED; the Redis-published verdict typically arrives within one anomaly-detector poll cycle (~10 s).
panels.title: p95 latency vs DEGRADED threshold

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  time_bucket('$__interval', time) AS "time",
  instance AS metric,
  percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY value) AS value
FROM metrics
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
  AND service = 'load-balancer'
  AND metric_name = 'request_latency_ms'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Error rate per backend with the 5% UNHEALTHY line. The threshold engine publishes UNHEALTHY (not DEGRADED) when error_rate crosses this, and the lb-sidecar excludes the backend from the upstream pool on the next anomaly publish.
panels.title: Error rate vs UNHEALTHY threshold

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  time_bucket('$__interval', time) AS "time",
  instance AS metric,
  AVG(value) AS value
FROM metrics
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
  AND service = 'load-balancer'
  AND metric_name = 'error_rate'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Time each backend spent in each derived state across the visible window. 'degraded_s' and 'unhealthy_s' are the durations from SOT §17.2 line 3287. The bucket width is held at 30 s in SQL so the column units are seconds regardless of the Grafana $__interval.
panels.title: Time-in-state per backend (visible window)

targets.rawSql:
WITH buckets AS (
  SELECT
    time_bucket('30 seconds', time) AS bucket,
    instance,
    CASE
      WHEN AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE metric_name = 'error_rate')         > 0.05 THEN 'unhealthy'
      WHEN AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE metric_name = 'request_latency_ms') > 200  THEN 'degraded'
      ELSE 'healthy'
    END AS state
  FROM metrics
  WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
    AND service = 'load-balancer'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT instance,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'healthy')   * 30 AS healthy_s,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'degraded')  * 30 AS degraded_s,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'unhealthy') * 30 AS unhealthy_s
FROM buckets
GROUP BY instance
ORDER BY unhealthy_s DESC, degraded_s DESC

panels.description: Anomaly-detector's official verdicts as persisted to the backend_health hypertable. This is what the sidecar's startup-hydration path (v1.0.7b G2) reads. If this table is empty for the visible window, the detector isn't persisting — the live Redis stream is still working but exclusions won't survive a sidecar restart.
panels.title: Latest backend_health verdicts (last 25)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, backend_id, status, score
FROM backend_health
ORDER BY time DESC
LIMIT 25

title: SmartLoad — Anomaly
